narratives.Description: Stories that share one completion issue (the first GitHub issue reference of each brief) compete for the same deft-story: N mark, and a part line cannot complete any of them, yet nothing says so until scope:complete refuses after merge (#6934). The worker envelope also asks the parent to pick a story line per task, so a leaf that delivers a whole story can carry deft-story-part: N (#6882 item 1). This story adds a warn-only shared-issue check to swarm:readiness, xbrief:preflight and swarm:launch, makes the envelope default to deft-story: N, and has the story-line writer note any part line on a product branch.
narratives.Overview:
1. Helper. In `packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/story-issue.ts`, a function returns, for one story brief, the other story briefs in `xbrief/pending` and `xbrief/active` (legacy `vbrief/` read-accepted) whose `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` names the same repository and issue. Epic and phase briefs are not counted. Files only, no forge. The #6468 case A check (`storyIssueIdentityMessage`) stays as it is and is not merged with this one.
2. Warning text, one per shared issue: "<rel> shares completion issue <repo>#N (each brief's first GitHub issue reference) with <rels>. Their product PRs would compete for `deft-story: N`: only the PR named by `metadata.productPullRequest` in its brief on the fetched delivery branch can complete, and an operator attestation does not get past another product part. Give each story its own issue as its first GitHub issue reference, or carry the work as one story."
3. `swarm:readiness`. `readinessReport` runs the helper for each story candidate and prints the warnings under a new heading "Shared story issues" ("- none" when empty). Exit code unchanged.
4. `xbrief:preflight`. `evaluate` runs the helper for the brief and appends the warning to the OK message, as it does for `placementWarning`. Exit code unchanged.
5. `swarm:launch`. When the gates pass, launch runs the helper for each resolved story (directly, not by parsing gate text), removes duplicates, and adds the warnings to the success stderr beside the existing advisory note. Stdout stays the JSON manifest; exit code unchanged.
6. Envelope. `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-ops.md`: the task line becomes `Task A (xBRIEF: [filename], issue #[N])`; STEP 5 and the rule at line 95 say the worker writes `deft-story: N` with `--write-story-line`, and passes `--part` only when the envelope says "split: a later product PR completes this story". `core-phase-3.md` line 151 says the envelope names the story issue, and names a split only for a split story. No launch-manifest story-line field.
7. Writer note. `writeStoryLineToBodyFile`: when the branch diff (`collectLocalDiffFiles`) is product-shaped (`isProductShapedDiff`) and the resulting body carries `deft-story-part: N` for a running story issue N of the branch, written now or already present, the OK message adds: "`deft-story-part: N` on a product PR: this PR does not complete story #N; a later PR with `deft-story: N` must. If this PR delivers the whole story, replace the line with `deft-story: N` (dropping --part does not remove a line already in the body)." Exit code unchanged; an existing line is never rewritten. `pre-pr:run` writes the writer's OK message to stderr whether or not `--json` is set, including when it goes on to start a controller run; stdout stays the controller JSON (`packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts` 670-674).
8. One PR. Files: `story-issue.ts`, `swarm/readiness.ts`, `preflight/evaluate.ts`, `swarm/launch.ts`, `pr-closing-keywords/main.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts`, their tests, `core-ops.md`, `core-phase-3.md`, one `changelog.d/` fragment. No new verb, flag, constant, policy field or refusal. None of the source files is a declared evaluator surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two story briefs in `xbrief/active` whose first GitHub issue reference is the same issue, when `swarm:readiness` runs on either, then the report lists both under "Shared story issues" and the exit code is what it would be without them.
- Given the same briefs, when `xbrief:preflight` runs on one, then it exits 0 and the message carries the warning naming the other brief.
- Given the same briefs, when `swarm:launch` runs on one story and its gates pass, then the warning is on stderr, stdout is the unchanged JSON manifest, and the exit code is 0.
- Given an epic brief and one story brief with the same first issue reference, then no warning is printed.
- Given two story briefs whose anchors name the same number in different repositories, or a sharing brief in `xbrief/completed`, then no warning is printed.
- Given a product branch of a running story, when the writer runs with `--part`, then it writes `deft-story-part: N` and prints the note.
- Given a product branch whose body already carries `deft-story-part: N`, when the writer runs without `--part`, then the body is unchanged and the note is printed.
- Given a brief-only branch, when the writer runs with or without `--part`, then no note is printed.
- Given a product branch whose body already carries `deft-story-part: N`, when `pre-pr:run --body-file <body> --json` runs without `--part` and starts a controller run, then the note is on stderr, stdout is valid controller JSON, the body is unchanged, and the exit code is 0.

## In plain English
A story completes when its merged product PR proves delivery to the story's issue. The issue is the brief's first GitHub issue reference (the "anchor"), and the normal proof is basis (a): exactly one merged non-brief PR whose merge-time body carries `deft-story: N`. When several stories anchor on one issue (12 child stories all pointing at their epic's issue, in the #6934 report), no story can complete in the normal way. If every PR carries `deft-story: N`, each PR is contested by the others. If every PR carries `deft-story-part: N`, each PR is a partial delivery, and the #6645 part-line route also fails because the other parts are product parts. Nothing before `scope:complete` notices this; the operator finds out after the PRs merged.

#6882 item 1 is the sibling failure on stories that did have one issue each: the parent wrote `deft-story-part: N` into each leaf's envelope, so each whole-story PR could complete only through an operator `delivery-identity-attest` grant (basis d). The envelope template still offers the parent a choice of line for each task.

The operator's goal for this arc: stories complete by construction, so the after-merge attest grant is never needed on the normal path, with fewer gates, not more.

The recommended fix: one shared check that reports stories sharing an anchor, shown as a warning (not a refusal) by `swarm:readiness` and `xbrief:preflight`; the worker envelope stops asking the parent to choose a line, so a leaf writes `deft-story: N` by default; and the story-line writer prints a note when `--part` is used on a product branch. One PR, no new verb, flag, constant or policy field.

## Operator direction (Scott, 2026-11-21, "Arc #6934"; relayed by the coordinator; recorded as constraints)
- Make stories completable by construction, so the basis (d) attest grant is not needed on the normal path.
- Fewer gates and steps. Refuse, or warn first as #6886 did.
- Keep the build to one PR if possible.

## Pains
- P1 — A cohort whose stories share one anchor issue passes `swarm:readiness`, `xbrief:preflight` and dispatch, but none of those stories can complete through its own PR. The failure appears only at `scope:complete`, after merge, and recovery costs new issues, a brief-retarget PR and a follow-up PR per merged story (#6934).
- P2 — A leaf that delivers a whole story can be marked `deft-story-part: N`, because the envelope template asks the parent to pick the line per task. That PR then completes only through an after-merge operator grant (basis d, #6645 route) or an extra PR (#6882 item 1).

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- `scope:complete` discovery of a `deft-story: N` PR: #6873 (arced, ingest-ready). This arc assumes its result and does not redesign it.
- The #6645 part-line attest route (merged in fc038d3b9, after v0.130.2; not yet released). It stays as the recovery path.
- #6544 (the closing-keywords check asks a brief-only PR for `deft-story: N`, not `deft-story-part: N`). This arc does not change which line a brief-only PR carries.
- #6937 (one mint approval per cohort).
- Completing stories already merged under shared anchors or part lines (recovery for the reporters).
- A later story on an issue whose earlier story already completed with a `deft-story: N` PR: that PR is a competitor forever. Detecting it needs a forge read; not here.
- Turning the warnings into refusals (a later release, as on #6886).

- #6882 item 1 (same consumer): seven stories, one issue each, every product PR carried `deft-story-part: N`; a lifecycle PR with seven `deft-story: N` marks was refused (not the sole mark; brief-only).
- #6882 triage comment 7048900748 maps item 1 to #6645.

Two stories can pass basis (a) despite competing marks if each candidate matches its brief’s `metadata.productPullRequest` on the fetched delivery branch. 3. **Warn.** The stamp exception makes an unconditional refusal too broad. A refusal’s strongest argument is prevention before immutable merge-time evidence exists, but it needs a predicate that distinguishes unsupported sharing from supported delivery identities. This design has not supplied that predicate.

4. **D5 improves the default but is insufficient by itself.** Keep the writer as the source of the issue number; no manifest line field and no blanket refusal of product `--part`. Extend D6 to diagnose relevant part-lines already present in the resulting body, including calls without `--part`.

5. **Exclude completed briefs from this first shared-live-anchor warning.** Their presence alone does not prove a competing merged product PR. A single child sharing its parent epic’s issue also does not prove a completion collision; where the parent owns that issue, reuse #6468’s existing ownership diagnostic. Otherwise describe parent-anchor detection as a separate advisory scope choice.

## In plain English
Problem: when several stories share one completion issue (the first GitHub issue reference of each brief), their product PRs compete for the same `deft-story: N` mark, and a part line cannot complete any of them either. Nothing says so before the PRs merge. Separately (#6882 item 1), the worker envelope asks the parent to pick a story line per task, so a leaf that delivers a whole story can end up with `deft-story-part: N` and then needs an after-merge operator grant or an extra PR.

What the critic found: the design is sound with two gaps and two framing fixes. Gap 1: `swarm:launch` drops the output of passing checks, so a warning in readiness or preflight never reaches a parent who launches. Gap 2: the story-line writer keeps a part line that is already in the body, even when called without `--part`, and reports success; so dropping `--part` from the envelope does not remove a part line a worker reused. Framing: shared issues make completion contested, not impossible (a `productPullRequest` stamp on the delivery branch can settle competing marks), and an operator attestation does not get past another product part. And warnings plus a safer default reduce the risk; they do not guarantee completion.

Solution this lean proposes: one file-only check finds the other open story briefs that share a story's completion issue. `swarm:readiness`, `xbrief:preflight` and `swarm:launch` show it as a warning, with the exit code unchanged. The envelope names the story issue and no longer offers a choice of line, so a leaf writes `deft-story: N` by default; `--part` is for a story the envelope marks as split. The writer adds a note whenever the resulting body of a product branch carries `deft-story-part: N`, whether it wrote the line or found it there.

What this adds: one helper, one warning in three outputs, one writer note, envelope text.

What it removes: the parent's per-task choice of story line, and the late discovery of shared completion issues (now shown before dispatch).

What it does not do:
- It does not refuse anything. Turning the warning into a refusal is a later release, as on #6886; the stamp route means a refusal needs a narrower rule than "shared anchor".
- It does not guarantee completion: a parent can ignore the warning and a worker can still choose `--part`.
- It does not change the live story-line check, CI, or which line a brief-only PR carries (#6544).
- It does not warn on completed briefs, or on one child story that shares its parent epic's issue.
- It does not change discovery (#6873), the #6645 part-line route, or mints (#6937).
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. Leftover next-build: none required; refusal and completed-brief detection are optional later work, not filed here.

## Summary
Validation, `swarm:readiness`, `xbrief:preflight` and `swarm:pre-dispatch` all accept a cohort of stories that share one origin issue, but no such story can ever be completed. The failure only appears at `scope:complete`, after the PRs have merged.

## Context
An epic with 12 child stories, each with `plan.references` / `metadata.origin` pointing at the epic issue (#1840 in the consumer repo). Following the dispatch doctrine, workers marked their PRs `deft-story-part: 1840`, because no single PR completes the epic issue. Three PRs merged.

## Expected behavior
Readiness, preflight or the activation step warns or refuses when several active stories share one origin issue, or when a story's origin is its own parent epic's issue. The warning should say each story needs its own issue (or a stamped `productPullRequest` plus a sole `deft-story: N` mark) to be completable.

## Actual behavior / gap
`deft scope:complete -- <story> --pr 1850 --merge-commit <sha>` refuses: `PR #1850 carries deft-story-part: 1840 ... is a partial delivery ... cannot complete the story on any basis, operator attestation included.` The merge-time body is immutable, so each merged story now needs an extra follow-up PR carrying `deft-story: <new issue>`. Recovery took creating 12 sub-issues, a brief-retarget PR and three follow-up PRs.

## Session notes
Related: the swarm SKILL's "Story line per story (#6316)" rule is correct, but nothing upstream checks that the story *has* its own N before dispatch.
